question: How is the input segmented in the original Transformer's translation experiments compared with H-Net?
final_text: I couldn't find this in the passages I retrieved from the three papers, so I won't guess. I searched: AIAYN §6.3 English Constituency Parsing; HNET §3.2 Alternate Language Datasets; AIAYN §1 Introduction; HNET §3.1 Language Modeling.
drafts: The authors' original Transformer translation experiments used a BPE‑based tokenizer (the Llama‑3 tokenizer) to segment inputs into subword tokens, whereas H‑Net processes raw byte inputs with a dynamic chunking mechanism that learns content‑ and context‑dependent segmentation jointly with the model [HNET:3.2:c061][HNET:abstract:c001].

Transformers use the Llama‑3 tokenizer which was designed for multilingual [HNET:3.2:c061]. H‑Net (space) and H‑Net (2‑stage) are byte‑level [HNET:3.2:c061]. The authors introduce a collection of new techniques that enable a dynamic chunking mechanism which automatically learns content‑ and context‑ dependent segmentation strategies learned jointly with the rest of the model [HNET:abstract:c001].
